![](/img/brochure.png){width=200 fig-align="center"}

A `{shiny}` app is a single page: one url, one UI, one server function. That is
comfortable while the app stays small. As soon as you want an actual site, with
a home page, a contact page, one page per user, urls people can bookmark or
send by email, you end up faking pages with tabs and `conditionalPanel()`, and
carrying the whole app in memory on every one of them.

`{brochure}` takes the problem the other way around: every page is a real page,
with its own url, its own UI, its own server function and its own Shiny
session. It is now on CRAN, in a stable 1.0.0.

```r
install.packages("brochure")
```

## A first app

You declare a `page()` with its own href, its UI, and a server function if the
page needs one. `brochureApp()` assembles them into an app you run like any
other.

```r
library(shiny)
library(brochure)

brochureApp(
  page(
    href = "/",
    ui = fluidPage(
      h1("Home"),
      plotOutput("plot"),
      tags$a(href = "/contact", "Contact us")
    ),
    server = function(input, output, session) {
      output$plot <- renderPlot({
        plot(iris)
      })
    }
  ),
  page(
    href = "/contact",
    ui = fluidPage(
      h1("Contact"),
      tags$p("No server function in this one.")
    )
  ),
  redirect(from = "/index.html", to = "/")
)
```

Navigate to `/` and to `/contact`. Moving from one to the other is a plain
link: the browser leaves the first page and opens a new session on the second
one. The home page runs its `renderPlot()`, and the contact page has no server
function, so nothing runs there.

## Urls that carry something

An href can hold a variable segment, and the page reads what it matched with
`get_keys()`: no argument inside the server, the `request` inside the UI.

```r
page(
  href = "/user/:id",
  ui = function(request) {
    fluidPage(h1(paste("User", get_keys(request)$id)))
  },
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    message("Serving user ", get_keys()$id)
  }
)
```

[`{routr}`](https://routr.data-imaginist.com/) handles the dispatch. A page can
also answer on a method other than `GET`, which is what you want for a form
post or a webhook.

## Doing things before Shiny

Between the moment a browser asks for a page and the moment it gets an answer,
`{brochure}` gives you two places to intervene: `req_handlers` run before Shiny
builds anything, `res_handlers` run on the way out. In `{shiny}` terms, this is
code that runs where no reactive context exists yet.

```r
brochureApp(
  page(href = "/", ui = tagList(h1("Home"))),
  req_handlers = list(
    function(req) {
      message(Sys.time(), " - ", req$PATH_INFO)
      req
    }
  )
)
```

A request handler that returns an `httpResponse` short-circuits: the response
is sent immediately and no Shiny session is created. That is how you serve
something that is not a page from inside a Shiny app, like a healthcheck for
your orchestrator, a webhook receiver or a small JSON endpoint.

## Carrying state between pages

Every page is a new session, so nothing computed on one survives a navigation
to another. State shared between pages has to be written down somewhere, and
the usual place is a cookie, set from a response handler and read back from the
page server.

```r
page(
  href = "/login",
  ui = tagList(h1("You are logged in")),
  res_handlers = list(
    ~ set_cookie(.x, "SESSION", "a-random-id", path = "/")
  )
)
```

`set_cookie()` defaults to `http_only = TRUE` and `same_site = "Lax"`, and
checks names and values against the character set cookies allow.
`vignette("cookies")` covers the whole pattern, logout included.

## Deploying it

A brochure app is a Shiny app, so it deploys like one. The part specific to
serving several urls is the prefix your app is mounted under: behind a reverse
proxy, on shinyProxy or on Posit Connect, `{brochure}` finds that mount, strips
it from incoming requests and prefixes the urls the app emits.
`vignette("deployment")` walks through the configurations.

## And with `{golem}`

If you build your Shiny apps as packages, `golem_hook()` turns a golem app into
a brochure app: it sets up the app object, creates a first page as a module,
adds `{brochure}` to your `Imports`, and writes a test for that page along with
the testthat structure to run it under `R CMD check`.

## What it costs

A brochure app is not a single page application any more, and that changes
things: a navigation is a full page load, nothing computed on one page is
available on the next, all pages share one R process, and a page that blocks
holds up every other page. `vignette("design")` says all of it, including when
*not* to reach for `{brochure}`.

## If you were running the GitHub version

1.0.0 rewrites the routing on top of `{routr}` and fixes a long list of bugs,
so a few things change on the way:

- `keys` is gone. A parameterised page used to read its matched values from a
  `keys` object installed in the global environment, invisible from a module, a
  golem app or any `local()`. Use `get_keys()`.
- `set_cookie()` has safer defaults (`http_only = TRUE`,
  `same_site = "Lax"`), and cookie values, domains, paths and redirect targets
  are validated rather than interpolated as is.
- `...` in `brochureApp()` is typed. It takes `page()`s, `redirect()`s, tags,
  tag lists, html dependencies and strings; anything else is an error. A bare
  list of pages is spliced, so `brochureApp(list(page_1(), page_2()))` builds
  two pages.

The [changelog](https://colinfay.me/brochure/news/index.html) has the rest.
